title: Specified finite dualizing coefficient and realization data
statement: Use the finite-field and finite-extension coefficient setting of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and the positive-level convention n+1. For a separated finite-type k-scheme X, choose the published compactification of its structural morphism. At level n, let G_n be the ordinary etale right adjoint for that compactification and W_n=G_n(A_n,s). The map u_mn is the transpose of inverse compact-support coefficient comparison, extension of the G_m counit, and the multiplication scalar-unit comparison. Its scalar adjunct is the semilinear transition. Let S_n be exact comparison pullback followed by the intrinsic finite-coefficient module equivalence. The specified intrinsic dualizing object is sfFiniteExceptional applied to the degree-zero regular intrinsic coefficient sheaf, and its origin isomorphism from S_n(W_n) is the boundary dualizing comparison with the regular scalar-unit normalization. The restriction square for S_n uses the comparison-site scalar restriction and intrinsic section-normalized restriction. Define the intrinsic semilinear transition by conjugating the realized scalar adjunct through that square and the origin isomorphisms; define the intrinsic finite comparison by transposition under extension adjoint to the actual normalized DVR restriction. Quotient maps are the actual ideal quotient factors; their identity and composition hold on residue representatives. All constructions and their unique section normalizations are those previously declared in lem-coef-finite-dualizing, unchanged.

proof.text: Use the published compactification, ordinary exceptional adjunction, scalar adjunction and proper/open coefficient maps to construct the ordinary comparison and its semilinear adjunct.

Construct the scalar restriction realization by the sheafification adjunction and its uniquely specified section generators; descend exact restriction to the derived localization. Conjugate by the normalized dualizing origins.
